newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close slightly down, red chips up.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close slightly down, red chips up.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended Tuesday's half-day trading session modestly lower, due to some cautious profit-taking, after clawing back most of the market's sharp early losses, brokers said.
"The market was down today because of the small headline fall in the Dow," said Chris Geiger, associate director at Vickers Ballas.
The Hang Seng Index closed 29.30 points lower at 13,451.45, after recovering from a 116-point drop at the open. Turnover was a healthy HK$5.46 billion, in line with Monday morning's HK$5.63 billion.
The exchange will not hold a session on Tuesday afternoon and will remain closed on Wednesday for the New Year holiday. Normal trading will resume on Thursday, January 2.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 11.54 points to 6,549.37, pushed down by program selling late in the session.
Geiger added many people have profits that they feel like taking out at this time.
While brokers noted the market has become more speculative, it appeared less vulnerable to sensitive political issues.
"The market is losing the Deng effect," said one broker with a large regional house.

A local Chinese-language newspaper report on Tuesday saying China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was taken to hospital last week was talked about in the market but did not appear to have any impact on trading, the broker said.
China related red chips and H shares led trade. Leading red chip and Hang Seng Index constituent CITIC Pacific fell HK$0.70 to HK$44.90, well off the share's record high of HK$46.40 set on Monday.
But Guangdong Investment put on HK$0.60 to HK$7.45 and China Resources added HK$0.55 to HK$17.40.
The H share sector outperformed the rest of the market with the sector index advancing 2.41 percent to 980.55.
The star performer was Guangdong Kelon, rising HK$0.35 to HK$5.00, followed by Qingling Motors, up HK$0.225 to HK$4.275.
The market's newest H share, Shandong Xinhua, which debuted on Tuesday, closed at HK$2.30, well above its issue price of HK$1.82.
Laggards, chiefly utilities, led the blue chip sector, followed by the commercial and industrial sector.
China Light jumped HK$0.40 to HK$34.40 and Hongkong Electric put on HK$0.30 to HK$25.70.
